name: Global surface folding analysis via convex hull ratio, alpha hull, and coarse-grained fractal scaling
purpose: Quantify global cortical gyrification as total pial surface area relative to a convex outer hull, and distinguish global hull ratio, alpha hull, FreeSurfer localGI, and anatomical inference, with source-stated comparability limitations.
species_scope: Mammalian (primates and other mammals) as supported by sources; not universally validated across all species.

inputs.statement: Pial surface mesh of the cortical ribbon.
inputs.quote: our proposed method requires the bounding pial and white matter surfaces of the cortical ribbon as input

inputs.statement: White matter surface mesh of the cortical ribbon.
inputs.quote: our proposed method requires the bounding pial and white matter surfaces of the cortical ribbon as input

inputs.statement: Point coordinates for convex hull computation.
inputs.quote: Coordinates of points to construct a convex hull from

inputs.statement: Cortical thickness estimate (average) for scaling law.
inputs.quote: we only had numerical values for the total and exposed surface area, as well a average cortical thickness estimates

conditions.quote: the analysis is always hemisphere-based, as in our previous work

conditions.statement: Coarse-graining erases morphological features smaller than the specified scale while preserving surface integrity.
conditions.quote: removes morphological details smaller than a specified scale while preserving surface integrity

conditions.statement: Isometric rescaling is applied to leave dimensionless shape properties unaffected.
conditions.quote: we apply an isometric rescaling process that leaves all dimensionless shape properties unaffected

steps.statement: Obtain pial and white matter surface meshes from MRI reconstructions.
steps.quote: We obtained these surfaces based on reconstructions from magnetic resonance imaging data in 11 different primate species.

steps.statement: Segment the space between pial and white matter surfaces into a 3D grid of boxes of desired scale λ.
steps.quote: we then segment the space between the original pial and white matter surfaces into a 3D grid of boxes of the desired scale λ

steps.statement: Apply isometric rescaling to coarse-grained outputs for analysis.
steps.quote: we apply an isometric rescaling process that leaves all dimensionless shape properties unaffected

steps.statement: Compute total surface area At(λ) and exposed surface area Ae(λ) at each scale.
steps.quote: we compare the total surface area At(λ) as a function of scale λ

steps.statement: Fit power law At(λ)T(λ)^(1/2) = k Ae(λ)^(5/4) to determine slope and offset.
steps.quote: all species followed a power law (linear regression R2>0.999 for all species); (ii) the slope of said power law is α=1.255

steps.statement: Compute convex hull of pial surface points using scipy.spatial.ConvexHull.
Extract hull surface area from the convex hull object.
steps.quote:
areafloat
Surface area of the convex hull when input dimension > 2.

steps.statement: Calculate gyrification index as ratio of total surface area to convex hull area.
steps.quote: The degree of folding is conventionally quantified by the gyrification index (GI), the ratio of the surface area to the area of the convex hull.

checks.statement: Quality check reconstructed surfaces by visual inspection.
checks.quote: These boundaries were then quality checked by visual inspection for particularly the young and old cohorts and manually corrected where needed.

checks.statement: Verify that coarse-grained cortices follow the scaling law with high R².
checks.quote: all species followed a power law (linear regression R2>0.999 for all species)

checks.statement: Check that K remains near-invariant across scales and species.
checks.quote: The variance in K across scales and all 11 species is <0.01

checks.statement: Ensure convex hull computation does not raise QhullError.
checks.quote:
QhullError
Raised when Qhull encounters an error condition

exceptions.statement: Coarse-grained brain surfaces are algorithmic outputs and not to be directly likened to actual brain surfaces in terms of fold location or shape.
exceptions.quote: the coarse-grained brain surfaces are an output of our algorithm alone and not to be directly/naively likened to actual brain surfaces, e.g., in terms of the location or shape of the folds

exceptions.statement: The model cannot capture large-scale features such as the longitudinal fissure, sylvian fissure, and specific gyri and sulci.
exceptions.quote: The shape of the mammalian brain has a number of prominent large-scale features: the longitudinal fissure, the sylvian fissure, and many specific gyri and sulci with important functional correlates that we cannot capture with our minimal model.

exceptions.statement: The mechanical model uses simplified geometries and material properties; real tissues may have stress-dependent growth and stress relaxation.
exceptions.quote: Real brain tissues are known to change their growth rates in response to stress (20), and other mechanisms lead to relaxation of elastic stresses over time.

exceptions.statement: The scaling law is empirical and does not specify the actual cortical shape beyond a constraint binding three morphometric parameters.
exceptions.quote: this universality, presumed to be arising from universal physical principles and evolutionarily conserved biomechanics, says little about what that cortical shape actually is, beyond a constraint binding three morphometric parameters

outputs.statement: Gyrification index (GI) as ratio of surface area to convex hull area.
outputs.quote: The degree of folding is conventionally quantified by the gyrification index (GI), the ratio of the surface area to the area of the convex hull.

outputs.statement: Fractal dimension df of the cortex, approximately 2.5.
outputs.quote: they each approximate a fractal with fractal dimension df=2.5

outputs.statement: Universal scaling law parameters: slope α and offset k.
outputs.quote: the slope of said power law is α=1.255 on a group level (CI: [1.254 1.256])
